title: Action Cards: pocketable on-call remediations and admin utilities
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: On-call engineers frequently need to execute small, safety-reviewed remediation actions (e.g. rotate a gateway key, clear a cache shard, restart a worker pool) without running a full procedural runbook. These ad-hoc actions are currently stored as free-form notes or partial scripts which creates drift, safety risk, and slow time-to-repair.

Goal: Build 'Action Cards' — concise, versioned admin utilities surfaced in the ops console and CLI that are executable as single Linear-style tasks. Action Cards are meant to be pocketable (quick to discover and run), safe (RBAC, dry-run option, preflight checks), auditable (immutable execution log, telemetry), and composable (can be chained or promoted into larger runbooks).

Scope & non-goals:
- In scope: UI surface in Console Quick Actions; a minimal Action Card schema; execution engine integration with existing admin-runlet runner; telemetry events; basic RBAC gating; CLI runner for quick keyboard-driven execution.
- Out of scope for this ticket: full authoring UX, a marketplace for cards, or long-running complex playbooks (these are follow-ups).

User stories:
1) As an on-call, I can search and run an Action Card to clear a model cache shard with a single confirmation and view the result in the Console.
2) As a platform engineer, I can create an Action Card that runs a safe sequence (preflight -> exec -> postcheck) and mark it as 'staging-only'.
3) As security/compliance, I can require 2FA for certain cards and review the audit trail for any execution.

Design overview:
- Card schema: id, title, description, tags, required_permissions, dry_run_command, exec_command, postcheck_command, timeout, allowed_environments, implied_dependencies, owner, created_at, version.
- Execution flow: 1) fetch card metadata; 2) evaluate preflight (permissions + optional dry-run); 3) present human-readable summary and risk level; 4) execute on selected environment via Admin Runner (existing short-lived ephemeral sidecar); 5) run postcheck and emit telemetry and audit entry.
- Safety controls: RBAC mapping to existing IAM roles, optional approvals for high-risk cards, circuit-breaker to prevent repeated executes on same target within window.

Technical approach:
- Backend: extend admin-runlet service to accept a new exec payload type 'action_card:<id>:v1' and ensure idempotent execution path. Add preflight plugin hook.
- Store: Action Card manifests stored in ConfigStore (encrypted, versioned), with a lightweight index for Console search.
- Console: Quick Actions panel — search, view details, run/dry-run, see last-run metadata.
- CLI: small 'redwood admin card run <id> --env=staging --dry-run' shim that calls the same API.
- Telemetry & audit: emit structured events (card.exec.request, card.exec.result, card.exec.postcheck) to telemetry pipeline and write immutable audit rows to the existing audit-log table.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement Action Card schema and persistence layer with basic validation.
- Extend Admin Runner to execute cards for 'staging' and 'prod-readonly' environments.
- Console Quick Actions shows cards and supports run + dry-run flows.
- CLI shim implements run/dry-run and prints postcheck summary.
- Telemetry events emitted for each phase and audit entries created.
- Automated e2e test covering a simple safe-card (clear cache) including preflight/dry-run/execution/postcheck.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag rollout to internal SRE org. 2) Collect feedback and telemetry for 2 weeks. 3) Expand to internal platform teams. 4) After QA and security review, flip flag org-wide with 2FA gating for high-risk cards.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- Existing one-off scripts remain supported; provide a migration CLI to convert approved scripts into cards with auto-suggested metadata.

Open questions & trade-offs:
- Where to draw the line between Action Cards and full runbooks? We choose single-step or short multi-step actions (<5 steps). Longer flows should become runbooks.
- Storage: use ConfigStore for fast iteration; long-term we may migrate manifests to a dedicated cards DB for query scaling.
- Approval UX complexity vs time-to-ship: start with email/Slack approval and evolve to in-console multi-approver flows.

Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/Action-Cards-Design (internal)
- Prototype CLI PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/admin-runner/pull/412
- Telemetry dashboard (example): https://grafana.redwood.example/d/card-exec-summary

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the safety model and telemetry semantics. The preflight hook must be extensible for future policy checks (quota, change-risk estimation).
comments: 2026-02-19 - Kickoff: internal SRE stakeholders (Maya, Jorge) validated the scope. Decided to limit to short actions to avoid scope creep.
2026-02-25 - Spike complete: prototype CLI runs via admin-runlet using existing ephemeral worker. Found race in postcheck ordering; added enforced sequencing in design.
2026-02-28 - Security sync: team requested 2FA gating for 'danger' tagged cards and audit retention policy. Security asked for explicit owner field and quarterly review label.
2026-03-03 - UX review with Product: Console Quick Actions mockups ok; asked to add last-run status and ability to view raw logs inline.
2026-03-06 - Engineering PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/admin-runner/pull/412 — covers new exec payload and preflight hook. Requesting review from @s-carter and @nguyen.

2026-03-10 - Implementation update: Backend exec path and persistence implemented; wiring to Console done for staging. Running e2e tests nightly; one flaky test on circuit-breaker observed and under investigation.
